feedback: Approved to race as a clean single-variable test. The candidate keeps the iteration 3 design, the best raced so far at 342.03, which has the sensors at x = -0.05, -0.025, 0, 0.025, 0.05. The only change is that every sensor moves forward from y = 0.05 to y = 0.07. Iteration 4 showed that widening the outer sensors to ±0.07 hurt (271.70, oval finish rate 0.6, s-bend progress 0.17), so the x spread stays at ±0.05. Iterations 0 to 2 showed max_error fixed near 0.061 to 0.065 whatever kp, ki, kd or base_speed were, and iteration 3 showed kd 0.4 cut oval max_error to 0.043. That leaves sensor lead as the untested lever on the tight tracks, so this candidate targets the right limit. Read the result in this order. (1) If s-bend and slalom line_loss_events fall and their progress rises above 0.3, keep y = 0.07 and then test sensor_size 0.016 at the same positions. (2) If the oval finish rate drops below 0.8 or oval steering_oscillation rises above about 0.3, the forward shift is making the sensors react to noise, so return y to 0.05 or try kd 0.3 before further geometry change. (3) If the s-bend and slalom results are essentially unchanged, lead distance is not the limit, so the next test should be the sensor footprint.
requested_changes: If s-bend and slalom line_loss_events fall but max_error stays near 0.06, keep the iteration 3 x spread (±0.05, ±0.025, 0) and try geometry.sensor_size 0.016 at y = 0.07, since iteration 3 showed the tape is lost on sharp bends and the larger footprint sees more of it.

If oval finish rate drops below 0.8 or oval steering_oscillation rises above about 0.3 with y = 0.07, return every sensor to y = 0.05 and set controller.kd to 0.3, since iteration 3 showed kd 0.4 gave the oval its finish-rate gain and kd 0.2 in iteration 2 gave none.

If the s-bend and slalom progress is unchanged, do not move the sensors further forward. Keep the iteration 3 geometry and try controller.base_speed 1.4 with kd 0.4, since iteration 3 showed the tight tracks are limited by line loss, not by speed, and max_error did not move with speed in iterations 0 to 2.
